target.title: feat(ledger): add immutable action history core
target.body:
## Summary

- add immutable, create-only JSONL action shards with deterministic replay and conflict detection
- restrict all identity inputs to strict canonical JSON; lossy values, object subclasses, accessors, sparse arrays, cycles, and credential-shaped fields are rejected
- require explicit outcome-independent idempotency identities for mutations so failed-to-completed retries keep one business identity
- reject symlink or junction traversal for spool, shard, partition-marker, source-import, and destination-import paths
- enforce a bounded machine-text privacy vocabulary for GitHub tokens, JWT-like values, bearer/API credentials, private hosts, private paths, and high-risk credential fields
- derive shard partitions only from immutable workflow run metadata or an explicit stable date
- bind repository and SHA into producer identity and shard paths
- preserve source timestamps while deterministically sorting causal children after parents
- keep CrabFleet projection failures durable without logging response bodies

## Design

- local writers spool one immutable event file per transition
- workflow finalization batches events into one digest-addressed shard per full producer identity
- shard paths are `ledger/v1/events/YYYY/MM/DD/<producer-repo>/<producer>/<run-attempt-job-digest>.jsonl`
- mutations require an explicit idempotency identity that excludes status, reason, and outcome
- source timestamps remain evidence; causal topology breaks ordering conflicts inside a shard
- mutable comments, dashboards, sessions, command ledgers, and evidence graphs remain projections, not the source of truth

## Validation

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false run build`
- focused `oxlint` on changed source and tests
- `node --test test/action-ledger.test.ts test/action-ledger-runtime.test.ts` (`49/49`)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false run check` (unit, repair, coverage, lint, TypeScript, and formatting all passed)
- schema/runtime privacy differential coverage
- concurrent flush, replay reconstruction, causal ordering, cross-repository identity, and source/destination symlink coverage

## Follow-ups

- instrument review/apply and sweep publication
- instrument command, repair, notification, and operational workflows
- bind review and closure evidence to Gitcrawl snapshots and Cloudflare archive queries
- add deterministic projection rebuilds and retention compaction

target.title: perf(repair): stage validation proof gates
target.body:
## Summary

- plan repair validation as ordered, risk-aware proof stages and independently rebuild exact proof semantics before replay
- keep untrusted execution credential-free and lifecycle-script-free; bind immutable source, base, head, action, and output identities
- publish only exact independently validated commit and tree bytes through credential-scoped mutation jobs
- recheck live pause and structured security signals at every mutation boundary
- checkpoint replacement publication before irreversible source closeout and recover only the exact authorized replacement PR
- make retryable post-flight outcomes visible and durable for self-heal
- resolve rerun handoff artifacts by trusted producer artifact ID and digest instead of consumer attempt names
- reject unsafe command aliases and options, source mutation, proof drift, and terminal runtime budgets

## Final hardening

- revalidate every sealed issue and PR source in the shared guard immediately before privileged push/create/reopen/label/comment/close mutations
- allow source drift only for the exact prepared source head or a closure recorded by the verified publication checkpoint
- fail closed when a configured canonical changed-gate script disappears
- allow only narrow read-only package-manager proof forms; reject lifecycle, registry, and account mutations across pnpm, npm, Bun, and Yarn
- keep deadline-expired pending or missing checks retryable for durable self-heal
- snapshot ignored dependency/tooling inputs and symlink targets around every staged proof command
- verify every applicable strict ruleset, including bypass actors and the full effective required-check set
- bind issue-implementation readiness to the exact head in the verified publication receipt

## Validation

- exact head: `d4e6e7db6052acaae628c9f1713ea4f52d46b428`
- Node 26.5.0 / pnpm 11.10.0
- focused hardening suites: execution handoff 25/25; post-flight 16/16; target validation 72/72; strict binding/post-flight 36/36
- full unit suite: 922/922 passed
- full repair suite: 839/839 passed
- changed coverage: 100% lines, 86.90% branches, 100% functions
- aggregate coverage: 73.17% lines, 72.19% branches, 83.26% functions
- direct `pnpm run check` equivalents passed: active-surface and limits checks, all three TypeScript builds, all four lint lanes, unit and repair suites, changed and aggregate coverage, and formatter check on 350 files
- the pnpm script wrapper refused before execution because it attempted a non-TTY reinstall of the shared `node_modules` (`ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY`); no install or dependency replacement was performed
- GitHub checks: 6/6 passed, including `pnpm check`, CodeQL for Actions and JavaScript/TypeScript, and the Windows Codex launcher

target.title: ci(cloudflare): deploy crawl-remote from protected ClawSweeper environment
target.body:
## Summary

- split crawl-remote production deployment into an unprivileged preflight runner and a fresh protected deployment runner
- require the selected SHA to equal the current `openclaw/crawl-remote` `main` tip during preflight, before D1 mutation, and again after migrations immediately before Worker deployment
- build and test the exact target SHA without production credentials, then upload only a prebuilt single-file Worker bundle, sanitized Wrangler config, D1 migrations, and a canonical SHA-256 manifest
- fail closed unless Wrangler dry-run emits exactly one regular deployable file named `index.js`
- bind artifact and receipt identity to run ID, run attempt, target SHA, and validated `observation_order_state` (`dormant` or `active`), and retain the artifact for 31 days so it survives the protected-environment approval window
- run the protected job with exact Node `24.18.0` and committed lockfile-backed Wrangler `4.107.1`; it checks out only the trusted ClawSweeper toolchain at `${{ github.sha }}` and never checks out or executes crawl-remote code
- prove the selected D1 fence state before and after migrations, deploy the prebuilt bundle with the exact release SHA, and poll both workers.dev and `reports.openclaw.ai/crawl-remote` until their health and contract endpoints advertise the exact release and selected capability state

## Final reviewer fixes

- run `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` from inside `.github/deploy/crawl-remote-toolchain`; the focused test executes the extracted workflow install against a copied lockfile-backed toolchain
- split D1 mutation and Worker deployment into separate credentialed steps, with a token-only exact-current-main reauthorization directly between them
- parse Wrangler `4.107.1`'s structured D1 `APIError` JSON: exact request path, `name`, `kind`, code `7500`, account tag, and a single exact missing-table diagnostic in `notes`; unrelated failures, extra fields, stderr, and active missing-table bootstrap fail closed
- reject extra Wrangler output modules, nested assets, symlinks, directories, and any bundle layout other than a sole regular `index.js`
- validate release identity and the complete contract independently through both the workers.dev origin and configured production route
- retain the release artifact for 31 days, covering GitHub's 30-day environment approval wait with a one-day margin

## Security boundary

- preflight has no GitHub environment or Cloudflare credential and mints only an exact-repository `Contents: read` App token for `openclaw/crawl-remote`
- deploy runs under `crawl-remote-production` on a fresh runner with `contents: read`, `bash --noprofile --norc`, cleared shell startup channels, and no target lifecycle/test execution
- deploy sparsely checks out only `.github/deploy/crawl-remote-toolchain` from `openclaw/clawsweeper` at `${{ github.sha }}`, with persisted credentials disabled
- only the locked toolchain Wrangler binary may query or mutate Cloudflare resources
- the only Cloudflare secret reference is the environment-specific `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`; there is no repository-secret fallback
- an existing `remote_capability_fences` row must exactly match the selected dormant/active state before migrations; a pinned-shape missing-table API error is accepted only for dormant bootstrap
- the verified artifact is bounded by an exact file allowlist and hashes, and its receipt is consumed once before the first mutation
- workflow reruns remain forbidden; a fresh retry must package and deploy the then-current crawl-remote `main`

## Validation

- exact validated branch head: `bd2a58a829e5b19bffd6c9199afa2dc7fe9cf005`
- focused deployment/action tests: 19/19
- executable adversarial coverage for unsupported Wrangler output modules/assets, cross-origin stale release identity and malformed contracts, real locked toolchain installation, non-current SHA authorization, `main` advancing after D1 migrations, artifact tampering/extras/cross-state reuse, target-controlled execution, realistic Wrangler missing-table `APIError`, unrelated API failures, and strict post-migration fence state
- extracted workflow install with Node `24.18.0` and npm `11.16.0`: Wrangler `4.107.1` installed and verified
- ShellCheck on every workflow `run` block
- `PATH=/private/tmp/clawsweeper-corepack/node_modules/.bin:$PATH pnpm run check`
- crawl-remote merged `main` `d6bb9b7a9c7eff0704dab4845a00e1863b7b8ef1` with Node `24.18.0` and npm `11.16.0`: install, typecheck, 73 tests, Wrangler `4.107.1`, and deployment dry-run
- formatting and `git diff --check`

## Rollout

1. Dispatch must use the current exact `openclaw/crawl-remote` `main` tip; it is currently `d6bb9b7a9c7eff0704dab4845a00e1863b7b8ef1`.
2. The `crawl-remote-production` environment was verified on July 12, 2026 with administrator bypass disabled, required `openclaw/maintainer` approval, self-review prevention enabled, and a custom deployment branch policy allowing only ClawSweeper `main`.
3. `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is still absent from the environment. No rollout was attempted. Before the first deployment, bootstrap it only as an environment secret; do not create a repository fallback.
4. Restrict that custom Cloudflare token to account `91b59577e757131d68d55a471fe32aca` and zone `openclaw.ai`: Account Settings Read, Workers Scripts Edit, Workers R2 Storage Edit, D1 Edit, Workers Routes Edit for the zone, User Details Read, and Memberships Read.
5. Dispatch the first rollout with `observation_order_state=dormant`. After the D1 cutover fence is deliberately activated, future releases dispatch with `observation_order_state=active`.
6. Do not rerun an existing workflow attempt. After a partial failure, use a fresh dispatch for the current crawl-remote `main` tip.

target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.
